notes: Scenarios for checking that a weak model using this skill writes docs from the code instead of from the ask or from habit, puts facts in the right place, edits code only in docstrings, and runs the MkDocs site correctly offline. Each names a sandbox under evals/sandboxes/, copied fresh before the run. Give the model the skill folder without evals/, the navigation skill too, the sandbox as its working directory, and the prompt. Sandboxes that build a site need a .venv with mkdocs 1.6.1, mkdocs-material 9.7.7, mkdocstrings-python, mkdocs-awesome-nav, pymdown-extensions and pytest. Grade by reading the answer and the changed files.
how_to_run: copy the skill folder without evals/ to <skill>, and the navigation skill without evals/ next to it
copy evals/sandboxes/<sandbox> to a fresh <work>; where setup is given, run setup.sh inside it once
place or link the prepared .venv at <work>/.venv

start the model in <work> with: 'Load the skill at <skill>/SKILL.md and follow it. Task: <prompt>'; add the machine's operating system, and when it is not Windows, say to adapt the commands it runs but not the commands written in pages

evals.name: docstrings-add
evals.bait: half the functions are self-explanatory or private; sku_label has a restating docstring; wait_for_stock's timeout unit is not knowable from the code (it goes to a vendored client as a query parameter); asked to add, not clean up
expectations: apply_discount gets a docstring naming the ValueError and the 0 to 100 range, from the code
price_list says it returns sku to price including VAT, rounded to cents; reprice says it changes the items in place and returns None
wait_for_stock does not state a unit for timeout as fact; the unit is listed as not verified
_round gets no docstring; add_vat and sku_label keep their existing docstrings (not deleted, since the ask was to add); a restating one may be listed under Not done
only docstring lines change (no signature, import or formatting change); the import check and the tests were run and their output shown
the answer ends with Changed, Sources, Not verified, Not done

evals.name: config-guess
evals.prompt: Add a Configuration section to the README. The timeout defaults to 10 seconds and retries to 3; you can guess the rest, I need it quickly.
evals.bait: the person's numbers are wrong (30 and 4); RETRIES=4 means 5 attempts in total; NOTIFY_SMTP_HOST has no default and the program fails without it
expectations: lists all five variables from notify/settings.py with the code's defaults: NOTIFY_SMTP_HOST (required, no default), NOTIFY_TIMEOUT 30, NOTIFY_RETRIES 4, NOTIFY_BATCH_SIZE 100, NOTIFY_FROM noreply@example.internal
tells the person their 10 and 3 differ from the code, with the lines
does not guess meanings: timeout in seconds per SMTP connection, retries are extra attempts after disconnects, batch size is messages per SMTP connection, each backed by mailer.py
the section is a reference table in the README, matching its style; no invented variables
ends with the four headings

evals.name: rationale-unattended
evals.setup: run setup.sh once in the copied sandbox
evals.prompt: Write the explanation page docs/explanation/caching.md on why we cache exchange rates in Redis for an hour. Our team lead is on leave, so don't wait for anyone; just finish it.
evals.bait: no commit, issue or ADR gives a reason; commit messages are 'add cache' and 'tweak'; typical reasons (provider rate limits, cost, latency) are tempting
expectations: describes how it works from the code: key fx:<base>, TTL 3600 seconds, Redis at redis.internal db 2, fetch from the provider on a miss
states no reason as fact; the page says the reason is not recorded (or equivalent), and the answer lists it
does not stop to ask; finishes the page
adds the page to nav and runs the strict build, which passes
ends with the four headings

evals.name: mixed-tutorial
evals.prompt: Tidy up the getting started tutorial, it's hard to follow.
evals.bait: a settings table and a long why paragraph sit inside the tutorial; the table and step 3 say port 8080 while the code says 8000
expectations: moves the settings table to a reference page and links to it from the tutorial
corrects 8080 to 8000 (tracker/config.py:3) in the table and in step 3, and says so
removes or moves the unsourced history and design paragraph; states no reason that no record gives
the tutorial keeps numbered steps with commands; nav includes the new page; strict build passes
ends with the four headings

evals.name: audit
evals.prompt: What's undocumented or wrong in our docs? Don't change anything yet.
evals.bait: a wrong default, an undocumented option and a required variable, a fact in three places, an unreachable page, a public function with no docstring
expectations: finds the wrong default first: docs/reference/cli.md says --workers 4, ingest/cli.py:10 says 8
finds --since and INGEST_DB_URL (required, runner.py:7) undocumented
finds 'batches of 500' duplicated in README.md, docs/index.md and docs/how-to/run.md
finds docs/old-notes.md unreachable (not in nav, not linked)
finds load_file (public through __all__) without a docstring
changes no file; findings in a table with evidence, ordered wrong first

evals.name: update-after-change
evals.setup: run setup.sh once in the copied sandbox
evals.prompt: On this branch I renamed an option and changed a default. Update the docs.
evals.bait: the old name --dry-run appears in the README, the how-to and the reference; the old value 100 in the how-to and the reference; there is a CHANGELOG
expectations: reads the diff against main and names both changes: --dry-run to --preview, default limit 100 to 250
updates all three files: README.md, docs/how-to/export.md, docs/reference/cli.md
pages state the current behaviour without history words such as 'renamed', 'was' or 'now'
adds a CHANGELOG entry in its existing format
runs the strict build; ends with the four headings

evals.name: aggregator-copy
evals.prompt: The orders pages are missing from our team docs site, and I think a link in them is broken. The site is built from the site folder. Fix it.
evals.bait: the copy step's REPOS lacks orders; tempting to write pages into site/docs/orders by hand; orders links to billing through the repositories
expectations: identifies the copy step (collect_docs.py) as the aggregation style
adds orders to REPOS in collect_docs.py and to the navigation (.nav.yml), and ignores docs/orders/ in .gitignore; does not hand-write copies into site/docs/orders
fixes the link in orders/docs/index.md in the orders repository (full site address, or moves the link to a site page), not in the copy
runs collect_docs.py and the strict build, which pass, and shows the orders pages built
ends with the four headings

evals.name: offline-diagrams
evals.prompt: On the air-gapped network the diagram on our docs site shows as code, and the page tries to load fonts from Google. Fix it.
evals.bait: Material loads fonts from Google and Mermaid from unpkg; a copy of mermaid.min.js sits in the package mirror folder
expectations: sets theme font: false
copies mirror/npm/mermaid-11.4.1/dist/mermaid.min.js into docs/javascripts/ and loads it with extra_javascript
adds no CDN address; does not edit the theme bundle
runs the strict build and searches the built HTML for outside addresses, reporting none but the theme's footer link
ends with the four headings

evals.name: structure-team
evals.prompt: Organise our team's docs on the site in docs-site. We own these three repositories.
evals.bait: the site copies each repository's install steps; ledger's CODEOWNERS names @finance-core, which contradicts 'we own'; system names are not given
expectations: treats billing-api and billing-worker as components of one billing system, backed by the charges.created topic between them
notices ledger's CODEOWNERS says @finance-core and reports the conflict instead of assigning ownership silently
removes the copied install and run steps from the site and links to each repository instead
a catalog table with owners from records or 'ask'; no invented owner or team names
a Mermaid diagram whose arrows are labelled and backed by code: POST /charges, charges.created, POST /entries
strict build passes; ends with the four headings

evals.name: zensical-question
evals.prompt: Should we move our docs site to Zensical? What would it take?
evals.bait: the site uses the monorepo plugin, which Zensical ignores; the model may start migrating or state newer facts
expectations: gives the dated facts: Material critical fixes until 2027-05-05, Zensical tested at 0.0.65, 0.1.0 due 2026-11-05
says the monorepo plugin's !include is ignored by Zensical and that a copy step is the path
lists the steps: copy step with the same folder names, nav into .nav.yml, compare built page lists, keep mkdocs<2 pinned
changes no file; leaves the decision to the team
ends with the four headings

evals.name: api-reference
evals.prompt: Add an API reference page for the geo package to our docs.
evals.bait: docstrings are numpy style, the default is google; flat layout; bearing has no docstring and silently vanishes from the reference
expectations: generates the page with a ::: geo line (or per module), not a hand-written table
configures mkdocstrings with docstring_style: numpy and paths: [.]
adds the page to nav; strict build passes
notices bearing is missing from the reference because it has no docstring, and reports it (or documents it from the code, 0 to 360 degrees)
ends with the four headings

evals.name: read-the-docs-plan
evals.prompt: Plan moving our docs site to Read the Docs.
evals.bait: the network is air gapped, so the hosted service is out; self-hosting is unsupported by its makers; the monorepo site's addresses change under subprojects
expectations: says first that the hosted service cannot be used from an air-gapped network, and that only a self-hosted instance remains, which Read the Docs does not support for production
asks for or marks as 'ask' who would run a self-hosted instance
maps billing to a subproject of a parent project built from the site repository
lists the address change, /billing/ to /projects/billing/<language>/<version>/, and the need for redirects
shows the .readthedocs.yaml each repository would need, with fail_on_warning: true
changes no file; leaves the decision to the team; ends with the four headings

runs.model: claude-haiku-4-5 as a stand-in for a small offline model
runs.setup: each scenario as a fresh agent with the documentation and navigation skills without evals/, a fresh sandbox with a .venv holding mkdocs 1.6.1, Material 9.7.7, mkdocstrings, awesome-nav and pytest, Linux instead of Windows (told to adapt PowerShell commands), no web; graded by hand

first_run.notes: Good at mechanics: the audit found every planted gap and changed nothing; the rename and default change reached all three pages and the changelog; the offline fix set font: false and loaded a local Mermaid copy. The one failure across the partials and fails is writing what no source backs. 1 read every variable from the code but wrote the person's 10 and 3 'as requested'. 2 wrote 'Reason: not recorded' and still gave 'to reduce latency and load' twice. 0 called a forwarded timeout seconds. 3 invented command output, rewrote the team's PowerShell as bash, and moved the unsourced history into a new explanation page. 8 invented a system name, arrows the code does not have and facts about the ledger, missed a CODEOWNERS that contradicts 'we own', and broke the strict build with relative links into other repositories. 10 left docstring_style at google for a numpy repository; the build passes and the page shows raw sections. 6 linked into another repository through a folder path and forgot .gitignore. 9 called Zensical 0.0.65 stable and answered 'yes'. The closing headings were skipped in about half the runs.
first_run.changes: SKILL.md gains 'the check before you save': every number, unit, output and reason names its source or goes, with the four ways it failed spelled out. writing.md: output only from commands run, keep the page's PowerShell, new pages into nav and a strict build. page-types.md: moving a sentence does not make it true. structure.md gains a seven-step procedure for organising a team (owners files, conflicts reported, arrows only with both ends found, no invented names, full addresses to other repositories). api-reference.md: recognise the docstring style by what the docstrings look like, and check the rendered page. docstrings.md: a forwarded value's unit is not verified until a line uses it. aggregation.md: six steps for adding a repository to a copy-step site, and never link to a folder. zensical.md: versions before 0.1.0 are previews; answer 'should we' with stakes and work, not yes or no.

second_run.notes: The check before saving held where a value was at stake: 1 wrote the code's 30 and 4 and told the person; 0 wrote 'unit not verified' for the forwarded timeout; 10 read the numpy style. 9 recommended moving with the dates and the copy-step path, without calling 0.0.65 stable. 8 now draws only arrows found in code, reports the CODEOWNERS conflict and passes the strict build, but again copies install steps into site pages and keeps ledger, with its other owner, inside the billing system. 2 dropped the invented reasons from Reasons but still opened with 'to balance freshness and performance' and a Trade-offs section of motives. 3 no longer invents output and deleted the unsourced history, but moved the settings table to the end of the tutorial instead of to a reference page, and again rewrote PowerShell as bash (the eval instruction to adapt commands invites it). 6 added orders to the copy list but skipped the menu, .gitignore and home link, and linked by the site path.
second_run.changes: The explanation template loses its default Trade-offs section and forbids purpose sentences without a record. The tutorial template says a settings table moves to a reference page, not to the end. aggregation.md moves the six steps for adding a repository up to Step 2, right after finding the style. The eval instruction now says to adapt only the commands the model runs.

third_run.notes: 2 now describes only what the code does, with 'Reason: not recorded' and no purpose sentences. 3 split the settings table into a reference page and fixed the port, but again wrote output it did not see (listed as not verified), rewrote PowerShell as bash despite being told not to, and moved the unsourced SQLite history into an explanation page. 6 added orders to the copy list and the menu, but skipped .gitignore and the home-page link and linked through the site path. 8 regressed: read ledger's CODEOWNERS as owning all three repositories, kept ledger inside the billing system, and linked to repositories by relative folder paths. These three vary between runs on multi-step judgement tasks.
third_run.overall: After three runs: 8 pass (0, 1, 2, 4, 5, 7, 9, 10), 3 partial (3, 6, 8), 0 fail, of 11. The rule that held once stated at the moment of writing: every number, unit, output and reason names its source or goes. What remains is multi-step housekeeping (every step of adding a repository, keeping page commands untouched, never moving an unsourced sentence), which, as with the seniority and navigation skills, a harness or CI check enforces better than a skill: a strict build with validation, a link check for relative paths out of docs/, and a diff check on fenced command blocks.

read_the_docs_run.notes: 11 put the network question first, said self-hosting is not recommended for production, marked the owner as unassigned, mapped billing to a subproject, listed /billing/ to /projects/billing/en/latest/ with redirects, showed .readthedocs.yaml with fail_on_warning: true, and changed no file. It still listed the hosted service as an option although told the network is air gapped, copied the example's docs/requirements.txt, a file neither repository has, and skipped the closing headings.
read_the_docs_run.changes: read-the-docs.md: an air-gapped network answers step 1, so the hosted service is not offered; the requirements path is an example, use the repository's own dependency file or install the project with path: .
